# Indiana Pacers 26/27 NBA Season Preview | Tyrese Haliburton Is Back, But Is He Full Strength?

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-10, 30:44. https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and Tony East (Locked On Pacers) preview the 2026-27 Indiana Pacers after a 19-win season ruined by injuries. Tyrese Haliburton returns from his June 2025 Achilles tear and a case of shingles. The GM expects him ready for opening night, but he will likely be eased in with about 30 minutes a game and limits on back-to-backs. Ivica Zubac replaces Myles Turner in the old Finals starting five. He brings rebounding and screening but almost no shooting, and Rick Carlisle will probably keep him around 30 minutes. The biggest questions are Haliburton's level, Zubac's fit in an uptempo system and whether Pascal Siakam can hold off aging. Tony predicts 47 to 48 wins and Josh says 46. Josh does not see Haliburton as a first-round draft pick, but thinks he could finish the season ranked 13th or 14th.

## Rules and methods

- [16:14](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=974) Recent Achilles returnees have mostly come back close to their old level. The old idea of an automatic 10% drop in production for the rest of a career no longer holds.
  > "the idea that the Achilles was a death nail and it meant an automatic 10% decrease in production"
- [14:45](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=885) Players returning from an Achilles tear rarely play full back-to-backs. Over the last 10 years basically only Wes Matthews did, and with heavily reduced minutes in the second game.
  > "for the last 10 years, like basically only Wes Matthews played backtobacks"
- [16:30](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=990) A full 12+ months off after an Achilles tear may help players come back stronger than a 9 to 11 month timeline.
  > "Not a 10 month, not an 11month timeline like a full period of being able to get back"
- [27:55](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=1675) Fewer teams will tank this season, so good teams will win fewer games and bad teams more. Recalibrate win totals and do not expect easy wins against bad teams in March.
  > "you're not going to get the March red carpet laid out for you from the bad teams."
- [28:31](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=1711) Teams without their own draft pick have no reason to sit players late in the season.
  > "we're not going to have teams deliberately sitting a bunch of guys down the way we had."
- [19:06](https://youtu.be/sfCe7fS9daM?t=1146) Under Rick Carlisle, expect low regular-season minutes for starters, especially starting centers.
  > "he has been very frugal in distributing minutes to starting centers."
